How Mustard Fillets a Fish (out of order but numbered)

Here's how I fillet up a Walleye nice and easy. The site posted out of order but whatever.

Step 0 is get your shit together, whatever knives you might need and a food surface to work on, I usually don't use the fish clamp board but it helped me keep one hand less slimy so I could use my phone camera.

Step 1 is to slice up under the front fins to the spine, I usually flip it over and do both sides at the same time.

Step 2 is to turn your knife and slice in with just the tip of the knife along the side of the spine passed the Dorsal fin just to the back fin.

Step 3 is to push your knife through down to and out the asshole, make sure your knife is above the spine and didn't go below it. Slide down until you are just barely connected to the tail, DO NOT GO ALL THE WAY AND SEPARATE IT. Leave it connected, it makes a great handle for skinning later on.

Step 4 is to move back up towards the head and deepen that shallow cut you made with the tip, spread the meat up and gently guide the knife down, on Walleye and some other species of fish there are a set of "pin bones" you'll feel your knife go through them, then just lightly guide the knife along the rib cage while spreading the meat so you just separate the meat off the rib bones, don't cut through the rib bones, just ride along them and spread the meat,until you get through to the belly.

Flip it over and repeat steps 1-4, and cut up the belly to separate the 2 sides, cut the sline off at the tail so you have 2 fillets joined at the tail.

Step 5 is to cut out the cheeks and pectoral fin(wings) and then you can throw that part away unless you want to use it to make soup stock, then you just rip out the gill plates and the guts and boil the rest. The brains and eyeballs are delicious boiled too. Not much really needs to go to waste.

Step 6 is to skin it, just grab that tail and use it as a handle, then lay the fillet on a flat surface and hold the knife firm at the tail and pull the tail towards you, move the fish not the knife and it'll separate nice and clean.

Step 7 is my bounty, the cuts inside the fillet are where the "pin bones" were, they are easy to find and remove, you can cut them out or tear them out like a zipper, you can even just leave them in and if you fry them at a hot enough temperature they pretty much just dissolve away.

Step 8 is the garbage.

And that's how I clean a Walleye, I also rarely ever use fillet knives, I have several, I just don't find they work as good as a Buck hunting knife.
